newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban sugar harvest reaches two-mln-tonne mark.
newsitem.headline: Cuban sugar harvest reaches two-mln-tonne mark.

text.p: Cuba reached the two-million-tonne mark in its current 1996-97 sugar cane harvest, which is expected to produce slightly more than last year's 4.45 million tonnes, official media said Friday.
The ruling Communist Party daily Granma said two million tonnes was reached Thursday, two days later than in last year's harvest.
However, the newspaper noted that this year, it had taken less cane to reach the mark -- in other words the current harvest was more efficient.
It also noted that whereas at this time last year some 148 of the country's total 156 mills were operational in the harvest, this year there were currently 137 mills working.
Authorities have said they expect only a modest improvement on last year's harvest, without giving a target. Experts have said production could be about 4.7 or 4.8 million tonnes.
Vice-president Carlos Lage said earlier this week that the harvest would be more efficient and less costly.
Last year's harvest halted a disastrous slide in the sugar sector that began at the start of the decade. Production slumped to a low of 3.3 million tonnes in the 1994-95 harvest.
